category: Curve Fitting Toolbox > Curve & Surface Fitting
description: Fitting parametric and nonparametric models to curve and surface data, defining custom model types and fit options, preparing and excluding data, and evaluating, differentiating and integrating the resulting fit objects.

tools.name: fit
tools.description: Fit a curve or surface to data using a library model name, a custom fittype, or an interpolant/smoothing-spline method. It returns a cfit or sfit object plus a goodness-of-fit structure containing SSE, R-square, adjusted R-square and RMSE. This is the main entry point of Curve Fitting Toolbox.
tools.usage:
fitobject = fit(x, y, fitType)
fitobject = fit([x y], z, fitType)
fitobject = fit(x, y, fitType, fitOptions)
fitobject = fit(x, y, fitType, Name, Value)
[fitobject, gof, output] = fit(___)

parameters.name: fitType
parameters.description: Library name ('poly2', 'exp1', 'gauss3', 'fourier2', 'power1', 'rat23', 'sin1', 'smoothingspline', 'linearinterp', 'cubicinterp', 'lowess', 'loess') or a fittype object.

parameters.name: fitOptions
parameters.description: A fitoptions object, or name/value pairs like 'StartPoint', 'Lower', 'Upper', 'Robust', 'Weights'.

parameters.name: 'Exclude'
parameters.description: Logical vector or index list of points to leave out of the fit.

parameters.name: gof
parameters.description: Structure with sse, rsquare, dfe, adjrsquare and rmse.

tools.notes: For surfaces pass a two-column predictor matrix and use types such as 'poly23', 'loess' or 'thinplateinterp'.

tools.name: fittype
tools.description: Create a fit type object describing a model, either by naming a library model or by writing a custom equation as a string or function handle. You can declare which symbols are coefficients, which are independent variables and which are fixed problem parameters. Pass the result to fit to perform the actual fitting.
tools.usage:
ft = fittype(libraryModelName)
ft = fittype(expression)
ft = fittype(expression, Name, Value)
ft = fittype(@(a, b, x) ...)

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: Model equation as a character vector, e.g. 'a*exp(-b*x) + c'.

parameters.name: 'independent'
parameters.description: Name(s) of the independent variable(s), default 'x' (and 'y' for surfaces).

parameters.name: 'coefficients'
parameters.description: Cell array naming the fitted coefficients.

parameters.name: 'problem'
parameters.description: Names of parameters supplied at fit time and held fixed.

parameters.name: 'dependent'
parameters.description: Name of the response variable.

tools.notes: Custom nonlinear models almost always need a sensible 'StartPoint'; without one the fit may not converge.

tools.name: fitoptions
tools.description: Create or modify the options structure that controls a fit: algorithm, starting values, coefficient bounds, robust weighting, tolerances and smoothing parameters. Building it separately keeps a complicated fit readable and lets you reuse settings across datasets. Its available fields depend on the fitting method.
tools.usage:
opts = fitoptions
opts = fitoptions(libraryModelName)
opts = fitoptions('Method', methodName, Name, Value)
opts = fitoptions(ft)
opts = fitoptions(opts, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'Method'
parameters.description: 'NonlinearLeastSquares', 'LinearLeastSquares', 'SmoothingSpline', 'LowessFit', 'NearestInterpolant' and others.

parameters.name: 'StartPoint'
parameters.description: Initial coefficient values for nonlinear fits.

parameters.name: 'Lower' / 'Upper'
parameters.description: Coefficient bounds, which are often essential for physically meaningful fits.

parameters.name: 'Robust'
parameters.description: 'off' (default), 'LAR' or 'Bisquare' for outlier-resistant fitting.

parameters.name: 'Algorithm'
parameters.description: 'Trust-Region' (default) or 'Levenberg-Marquardt'.

parameters.name: 'MaxIter' / 'TolFun' / 'TolX'
parameters.description: Convergence controls.

parameters.name: 'SmoothingParam'
parameters.description: 0 to 1 smoothing parameter for smoothing splines.

parameters.name: 'Exclude' / 'Weights'
parameters.description: Excluded points and observation weights.

tools.name: cfit
tools.description: The curve fit object returned by fit for one-dimensional data. Coefficients are accessible as properties by name, and the object can be evaluated like a function, plotted, differentiated and integrated. Use coeffnames, coeffvalues, formula and confint to inspect it.
tools.usage:
f = fit(x, y, 'poly3');
y2 = f(xnew)
c = coeffvalues(f)
names = coeffnames(f)
str = formula(f)
plot(f, x, y)

parameters.name: f.<coeffName>
parameters.description: Direct property access to a fitted coefficient, e.g. f.p1 or f.a.

parameters.name: f(xnew)
parameters.description: Evaluate the fitted curve at new points.

tools.name: sfit
tools.description: The surface fit object returned by fit for two-dimensional predictor data. It is evaluated with two arguments, plotted as a surface, and supports the same coefficient inspection functions as cfit. Use it for response-surface models and 2-D interpolants.
tools.usage:
sf = fit([x y], z, 'poly23');
znew = sf(xnew, ynew)
plot(sf, [x y], z)
c = coeffvalues(sf)

parameters.name: sf(x, y)
parameters.description: Evaluate the fitted surface at given coordinates.

parameters.name: plot(sf, [x y], z)
parameters.description: Plot the surface with the data points overlaid.

tools.name: prepareCurveData
tools.description: Transform curve data into the column-vector form fit expects, converting to double, reshaping matrices and removing Inf and NaN entries. Mismatched shapes and stray NaNs are the most common cause of confusing errors from fit. Always run it before fitting data that came from elsewhere.
tools.usage:
[xOut, yOut] = prepareCurveData(xIn, yIn)
[xOut, yOut, wOut] = prepareCurveData(xIn, yIn, wIn)

parameters.name: xIn, yIn
parameters.description: Predictor and response data of any shape and numeric class.

parameters.name: wIn
parameters.description: Optional weights, reshaped and filtered along with the data.

tools.name: prepareSurfaceData
tools.description: Convert surface data into the column-vector form fit needs, expanding grid vectors into full coordinate lists and dropping non-finite values. It handles the common case where X and Y are grid vectors and Z is a matrix. Run it before any surface fit.
tools.usage:
[XOut, YOut, ZOut] = prepareSurfaceData(XIn, YIn, ZIn)
[XOut, YOut, ZOut, WOut] = prepareSurfaceData(XIn, YIn, ZIn, WIn)

parameters.name: XIn, YIn
parameters.description: Grid vectors or full coordinate matrices.

parameters.name: ZIn
parameters.description: Response matrix or vector.

parameters.name: WIn
parameters.description: Optional weights.

tools.name: excludedata
tools.description: Build a logical exclusion vector marking data points to leave out of a fit, by value range, index, box region or distance from a reference fit. Pass the result to fit through the 'Exclude' option. Use it to remove known-bad sensor readings or to refit after identifying outliers.
tools.usage:
outliers = excludedata(x, y, 'indices', idx)
outliers = excludedata(x, y, 'domain', [xmin xmax])
outliers = excludedata(x, y, 'range', [ymin ymax])
outliers = excludedata(x, y, 'box', [xmin xmax ymin ymax])

parameters.name: 'indices'
parameters.description: Logical vector or index list of points to exclude.

parameters.name: 'domain'
parameters.description: Keep only points with x inside the given range.

parameters.name: 'range'
parameters.description: Keep only points with y inside the given range.

parameters.name: 'box'
parameters.description: Keep only points inside the given rectangle.

tools.name: smooth
tools.description: Smooth response data with a moving average, lowess, loess, Savitzky-Golay or robust variant. Unlike fit it returns a smoothed data vector rather than a model object, which is what you want for denoising before further analysis. The span controls how aggressively the data is smoothed.
tools.usage:
yy = smooth(y)
yy = smooth(y, span)
yy = smooth(y, method)
yy = smooth(y, span, method)
yy = smooth(x, y, span, method)
yy = smooth(x, y, span, 'sgolay', degree)

parameters.name: span
parameters.description: Number of points (or a fraction of the data for lowess/loess) in the smoothing window.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'moving' (default), 'lowess', 'loess', 'sgolay', 'rlowess', 'rloess'.

parameters.name: degree
parameters.description: Polynomial degree for the 'sgolay' method.

tools.notes: The robust 'rlowess' and 'rloess' methods downweight outliers and are usually the safer choice for real data.

tools.name: differentiate
tools.description: Compute the first and second derivatives of a fitted curve or surface at specified points. Differentiating a fitted model is far more stable than differencing noisy raw data. For a surface it returns the partial derivatives with respect to each variable.
tools.usage:
fx = differentiate(fitobject, x)
[fx, fxx] = differentiate(fitobject, x)
[fx, fy] = differentiate(sfitobject, x, y)
[fx, fy, fxx, fxy, fyy] = differentiate(sfitobject, x, y)

parameters.name: fitobject
parameters.description: A cfit or sfit object from fit.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: Points at which to evaluate the derivatives.

tools.name: integrate
tools.description: Integrate a fitted curve numerically from a specified lower limit to each of a set of points. It returns the cumulative integral, which is useful for computing areas, totals and energies from fitted data. Only defined for cfit objects, not surfaces.

parameters.name: fitobject
parameters.description: A cfit curve object.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Upper limits at which the cumulative integral is evaluated.

parameters.name: x0
parameters.description: Lower limit of integration.

tools.name: confint
tools.description: Compute confidence intervals for the fitted coefficients of a curve or surface fit. Wide intervals or intervals straddling zero indicate a poorly determined parameter, often a sign of an over-parameterized model. The confidence level is adjustable.

parameters.name: fitobject
parameters.description: A cfit or sfit object.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Confidence level between 0 and 1 (default 0.95).

tools.name: predint
tools.description: Compute prediction or confidence bounds for the response of a fitted model at given points. 'functional' bounds describe the fitted curve itself while 'observation' bounds describe where a new data point would lie. Simultaneous bounds cover the whole curve at once rather than pointwise.
tools.usage:
ci = predint(fitobject, x)
ci = predint(fitobject, x, level)
ci = predint(fitobject, x, level, intopt, simopt)
[ci, y] = predint(___)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Confidence level (default 0.95).

parameters.name: intopt
parameters.description: 'observation' (default, new data point) or 'functional' (the fitted curve).

parameters.name: simopt
parameters.description: 'off' (default, pointwise) or 'on' (simultaneous).

tools.name: coeffvalues
tools.description: Return the fitted coefficient values of a curve or surface fit as a numeric row vector, in the order given by coeffnames. This is the convenient way to extract parameters programmatically instead of naming each property. Pair it with coeffnames to build a labelled result table.

parameters.name: fitobject
parameters.description: A cfit or sfit object.

tools.name: feval
tools.description: Evaluate a fit object at specified points, equivalent to calling the object directly as a function. It is useful in code that receives the fit object as a variable and cannot rely on the function-call syntax. Works for both cfit and sfit objects.
tools.usage:
y = feval(fitobject, x)
z = feval(sfitobject, x, y)
z = feval(sfitobject, [x y])

parameters.name: fitobject
parameters.description: A cfit or sfit object.

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: Points at which to evaluate the model.

tools.name: cftool
tools.description: Open the Curve Fitter app for interactive curve and surface fitting, with live comparison of model types, residual plots and goodness-of-fit statistics. You can exclude points by clicking and compare several fits side by side. Export the fit to the workspace or generate a reproducible MATLAB script.
tools.usage:
cftool
cftool(x, y)
cftool(x, y, w)
cftool(x, y, z)
cftool(fitobject)

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: Curve data to load into the app.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Response data for surface fitting.

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: Observation weights.

tools.notes: Requires a display. Use 'Generate Code' so the chosen fit can be reproduced in a script.
